About.title: About
About.body1: I'm Victor, a Berkeley student who goes to a lot of Bay Area tech events. Every week I pick the ones I'd actually recommend and say why in a line or two.
About.body2: You can see which ones I'm going to, filter by the categories you care about, and subscribe by calendar feed. Every page is in English and Chinese.
About.body3: No paid placements. Hosts can't buy their way onto this list.

Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.description: What Victor's Picks collects, what it's for, who handles it for me, how long I keep it, and how to have it deleted.
Privacy.lead: This is a small personal site, so this page is short and in plain words. Everything on it describes what the site does today.

who.title: Who runs this
who.body: I'm Victor, a Berkeley student, and Victor's Picks is my personal project. It has no ads and no paid placements.
who.noContact: A contact address for questions, data requests and takedowns will be added here before the email newsletter opens.

items.none: No ads, no analytics, no tracking pixels. The only outside code is Vercel's bot check, and it runs only when you press Subscribe.
items.sell: I never sell your data, and I don't share it with anyone except the services that run this site for me (listed below).
items.email: Your email address is used for the newsletter you asked for and nothing else.
items.leave: Every Sunday email has a one-click unsubscribe, and you can ask me to delete your data.

items.account: There are no accounts. Nothing asks for your name or email unless you subscribe.
items.cookie: One cookie, NEXT_LOCALE, and only if you use the language switch: it remembers English or Chinese for a year. My code sets no other cookies for visitors.
items.fonts: Fonts and images are served by this site, so your browser doesn't call Google Fonts or any other outside service while you read.
items.logs: Vercel, which hosts the site, keeps standard request logs (IP address, browser, the page requested) on its own schedule. I use them only to fix problems and stop abuse.
items.links: When you follow a link to an event page, that site only learns that you came from this site, not from which page.
items.feeds: Calendar feeds and RSS need no account. Their links carry only your language and category choices.

subscribe.title: If you subscribe

items.email: Your email address, the language and categories you picked, and your status (waiting for confirmation, subscribed, paused or unsubscribed) with its dates.
items.consent: The most recent sign-up request for your address, confirmed or not: when it was made, which page it came from, and the IP address and browser user-agent it was sent from. Once you confirm, that's the record that you asked to subscribe.
items.sends: Which weekly emails were sent to you, and when.
items.nothing: Nothing else: no name, no location, no browsing history.

subscribe.bot: When you press Subscribe, your browser runs Vercel's bot check (BotID), loaded through this site's own address, to tell people from scripts. It is Vercel's service, covered by Vercel's privacy policy.
subscribe.limits: To stop abuse I count sign-up attempts per network and per inbox. The counters hold a one-way hash of your IP address and of your email address, never the plain values, and expire within about 2 days.

use.title: What I use it for

items.send: Sending the confirmation email and the Sunday email, in your language and with only your categories.
items.abuse: Stopping bots, and stopping anyone from flooding someone else's inbox with sign-up emails.
items.proof: Showing that you asked to subscribe, and making sure an unsubscribe sticks.
items.nothing: Nothing else: no ads, no profiling, no selling.

use.ai: I use AI (Anthropic's Claude, through Vercel's AI Gateway) to help draft event summaries and translations. It only sees public event pages and my own notes, never your email address or anything else about subscribers or visitors.

items.none: I don't track whether you open an email or which links you click.
items.same: Every reader gets the same images, loaded from this site, and links go straight to their pages: no redirects, no tracking codes.
items.token: The only personal links are preferences and unsubscribe. They carry a code, never your address.

processors.title: Services that handle data for me
processors.lead: These companies run parts of the site for me.

items.vercel: Vercel hosts the site: request logs, the bot check, the firewall and image storage.
items.neon: Neon (part of Databricks) runs the database that holds subscriptions and send records.
items.upstash: Upstash keeps the rate-limit counters, which hold hashes only.
items.resend: Resend sends the emails. It sees your address, the email itself, and whether it was delivered, bounced or marked as spam.

processors.where: All four are US companies. The database and the counters are in the US East region.

items.pending: A sign-up that's never confirmed: deleted after 7 days. If you had subscribed before, it goes back to unsubscribed instead.
items.active: While you're subscribed or paused: kept.
items.unsubscribed: After you unsubscribe: kept for 12 months, so the unsubscribe sticks and the latest sign-up request is on record if a question comes up, then deleted along with its send records.
items.suppressed: Addresses that bounced, marked an email as spam, or that I blocked by hand: the whole subscription record, sign-up IP address and user-agent included, and its send records are kept indefinitely on a do-not-send list, so the address never gets email from me again. Resend also keeps bounced and spam-flagged addresses on its own do-not-send list. Both stay until you ask me to delete them.
items.limits: Rate-limit counters: about 2 days at most.
items.providers: Logs and backups at Vercel, Neon and Resend: deleted on each provider's own schedule (see their policies above). My own log lines never contain full email addresses.

items.prefs: Every Sunday email links to a preferences page where you can change the language or categories, pause for 4 weeks, or unsubscribe in one click, and your mail app's Unsubscribe button works on it too. The one-time confirmation email has neither: if you ignore it, nothing more is sent.
items.request: To see what I hold about you, or to have it deleted, email me from the address you subscribed with, at the address under “<contact>Who runs this</contact>”. Deleting removes your subscription and its send records from my database, and takes your address off Resend's do-not-send list if it's there. Copies in provider logs and backups expire on their own schedules.
items.suppressed: If your address is on my do-not-send list, it may be on Resend's as well. A deletion request takes it off both, so the block is lifted and you can subscribe again.
items.change: To change your address, subscribe with the new one and unsubscribe the old one.

signals.title: Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control
signals.body: I don't track you across sites, and no third party collects information about your activity over time and across different websites through this site. So Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control have nothing to switch off here: the site works the same whether or not your browser sends them. Either way, I don't sell or share personal information.

items.keep: For each pick I keep the public facts (title, time, place, host, link), a short summary in my own words, and sometimes a cover: the event's official cover image, credited as “Cover: host via platform”, or, when there isn't one, a tile made from the hosts' profile photos on the event page (credited in emails as “Host photos via platform”).
items.promise: If you host an event and want its cover (official or made from host photos) or its listing removed, email me at the address under “<contact>Who runs this</contact>”. Within 24 hours I'll swap the cover for a plain template or take the listing down, on this site and in future emails.
items.limits: Emails already sent, and copies kept by search engines or other sites, are beyond my reach.
items.inbox: Some picks start as invitations in my own calendars. Those wait in a private list only I can see, which keeps the title, time, place, links and a short snippet with email addresses removed (never the guest list), and are cleared a week after the event.

items.kids: This site isn't meant for children under 13, and I don't knowingly collect their information. If you think a child has subscribed, email me at the address under “<contact>Who runs this</contact>” and I'll delete it.
items.where: I run it from California for people in the Bay Area. It isn't aimed at readers in the EU or mainland China.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: When this page changes, the date at the top changes too. If a change affects what happens to subscriber data, I'll say so in the next Sunday email.

Subscribe.going: Subscribe to where Victor is going
Subscribe.urlHint: Paste into any calendar app that accepts a URL.
Subscribe.refresh: Calendar apps refresh on their own schedule: Apple in 15 minutes to a few hours, Outlook in 3–12 hours, Google in 12–24 hours or longer. Time changes and cancellations show up at the next refresh; a cancelled event stays in the feed, marked cancelled.
